$provenance: Vendored from https://github.com/adeyosemanputra/pygoat (OWASP PyGoat, MIT license) at pinned commit 19d17cc8874861142b330636d068bbde54e86b85 (2026-03-28). Trimmed to the `introduction` Django app (the OWASP Top-10 lab views) + project settings — the `challenge`, `chatbot`, and `dockerized_labs` sub-projects, migrations, and static assets were dropped as out of scope for static analysis. Every finding below was hand-verified by reading this exact vendored source, including the one template file needed to confirm the XSS sink (see corpus/README.md for the sampling method). `gt_pygoat_cmdi2` and `gt_pygoat_yaml_deser` were added after an initial real-pipeline scan surfaced them as apparent false positives in `introduction/mitre.py`/`introduction/views.py` (files already vendored for other findings) — re-reading both confirmed they are genuine, independently-exploitable vulnerabilities this pass had simply not catalogued yet, so they were added as true findings rather than left mislabelled. Do not "fix" these — they are the labels the precision/recall gate scores against.

expectedFindings.description: sql_lab builds `sql_query` by string-concatenating untrusted POST `name`/`pass` fields and executes it via `login.objects.raw(sql_query)` (Django ORM raw-SQL injection, PyGoat's A03 SQLi lab).

xss_lab passes untrusted GET `q` to the template as `query`; `introduction/templates/Lab/XSS/xss_lab.html:27` renders it with the `|safe` filter, explicitly bypassing Django's autoescaping (reflected XSS, PyGoat's A03 XSS lab).

cmd_lab builds a `dig`/`nslookup` command string from untrusted POST `domain` and runs it via `subprocess.Popen(command, shell=True, ...)` (OS command injection; the upstream protocol-prefix strip does not block shell metacharacters like `;`/`|`).

insec_des_lab base64-decodes a client-supplied `token` cookie and feeds it straight to `pickle.loads()` with no integrity check — a crafted pickle payload achieves arbitrary code execution (PyGoat's A08 insecure-deserialization lab).
xxe_parse explicitly enables `feature_external_ges` (external general entities) on a SAX parser before parsing the raw, unauthenticated request body (classic XXE, PyGoat's XXE lab).

ssrf_lab2 issues a server-side `requests.get(url)` where `url` is taken verbatim from POST body with no allowlist/scheme check, and echoes the response body back to the caller (SSRF, PyGoat's `ssrf_lab2`; note the similarly-named `ssrf_lab` at line ~926 is actually local path traversal, labelled separately below — file was scored on code behaviour, not PyGoat's lab name).

ssrf_lab (mislabelled by upstream as an SSRF lab) joins an untrusted POST `blog` filename onto a local directory with `os.path.join` and opens it with no traversal sanitization — arbitrary local file read.

a1_broken_access_lab_1 grants the admin-only secret whenever `request.COOKIES.get('admin') == "1"` — a client-forgeable cookie is trusted as the sole authorization decision, with no server-side session/role check.
Hard-coded Django `SECRET_KEY` committed to source control; rotation requires a human.
`DEBUG = True` in the project's committed settings — leaks stack traces, source snippets, and installed-app/settings details to any client on an unhandled exception if deployed as-is.

mitre_lab_17_api builds `command = "nmap " + ip` from untrusted POST `ip` and runs it via `command_out()`'s `subprocess.Popen(command, shell=True, ...)` — a second, independent OS command injection sink (MITRE ATT&CK ping-sweep lab), distinct from `gt_pygoat_cmdi`'s `cmd_lab`.

a9_lab loads an untrusted uploaded file with `yaml.load(file, yaml.Loader)` — PyYAML's full (non-safe) `Loader` reconstructs arbitrary Python objects from YAML tags (e.g. `!!python/object/apply`), a well-known arbitrary-code-execution footgun (PyGoat's A9 vulnerable-components lab, `get_version` on the next line even advertises "pyyaml v5.1"). Independent sink from `gt_pygoat_deser`'s pickle-based lab.
